evidence_summary: Layout +00 vftable / +04 Items / +08 Capacity / +0C IsInitialized / +0D IsAllocated / +10 Count / +14 CapacityIncrement(=10) re-derived from 8 independent .CRT$XCU initialisers (0xA8EB40, 0x8B4108, 0xA80228, 0xA8E390, 0x8B3DC0, 0xB0F720, 0xA8EC78, 0xA83DE8) AND, independently, from the arrays' own virtual methods (union of [this+disp] = {0,4,8,12,13,16}), AND from a literal inline insert sequence. Two unrelated code paths agree, so a single reading mistake cannot explain both.

0xA8EB40's static ctor installs 0x7E9E24, whose [V-4]=COL 0x801280 -> TD 0x823270 -> .?AV?$DynamicVectorClass@PAVBuildingClass@@@@. Therefore 0xA8EB44=Items and 0xA8EB50=Count of the *building* vector. No vftable store anywhere in the +-0x20 window of 0xA8EB44 introduces a UnitClass-derived type; the only other type in that window is DynamicVectorClass<VoxelAnimTypeClass*> at 0xA8EB28. 0xA8EB44 is therefore not a unit/object master table.

0x8B4108's static ctor (0x4E6C60..0x4E6C9E) installs vftable 0x7E9EA4, COL 0x8013B0 -> TD 0x823340 -> .?AV?$DynamicVectorClass@PAVUnitClass@@@@. Its +0x14 store is 0xA (0x4E6C87) and +0x10 is zeroed (0x4E6C91), exactly matching C1's offsets; the destructor restores the base VectorClass<UnitClass*> vtable 0x7E9EC4 at 0x4E6CA8. So 0x8B410C/0x8B4118 = vehicle Items/Count. The byte layout is identical to the BuildingClass vector's cluster, only 4 vftables apart, so the two readings cannot have been confused.

0xA80228's static ctor (0x4E6CE0..0x4E6D1E) installs 0x7E9EE4, COL 0x801448 -> TD 0x8233A8 -> .?AV?$DynamicVectorClass@PAVHouseClass@@@@, so 0xA8022C/0xA80238 are the House list. The aircraft vector is a separate object at 0xA8E390 whose ctor (0x4E6BE0..0x4E6C1E) installs 0x7E9E64, COL 0x801318 -> TD 0x8232D8 -> .?AV?$DynamicVectorClass@PAVAircraftClass@@@@, giving 0xA8E394/0xA8E3A0. The two bases are 0xE168 apart and are distinct static-ctor targets, so the "Aircraft" labelling of 0xA8022C in the project doc is indeed wrong.

The ELEMENT TYPE is right: 0xB0F720's static ctor (0x7252D0..0x72530E) installs 0x7E91EC, COL 0x8009B0 -> TD 0x8225E8 -> .?AV?$DynamicVectorClass@PAVAbstractClass@@@@. But the array is NOT an "all objects" registry. FootClass::FootClass at 0x4D31E0 (860 bytes, entry after the int3 pad at 0x4D31DB) provably installs .?AVFootClass@@ at [this] and touches FootClass::Array (0x8B3DC4 x1, 0x8B3DD0 x3) while containing ZERO references to 0xB0F724 or 0xB0F730. Of the 47 call sites of AbstractClass::AbstractClass (0x4101F0), only AlphaShapeClass, FactoryClass and one AnimClass destructor family ever inline a push; TechnoClass, BuildingClass, UnitClass, InfantryClass, AircraftClass, FootClass, BulletClass, AnimClass, OverlayClass, TerrainClass, SmudgeClass and HouseClass all call the ctor without registering. Reading [0xB0F730] as "all objects" therefore cannot be right.

0x8B3DC0's static ctor (0x4D3174..0x4D319E) installs 0x7E8C28, COL 0x800868 -> TD 0x822580 -> .?AV?$DynamicVectorClass@PAVFootClass@@@@, and the base-class destructor store is 0x7E8C48 (VectorClass<FootClass*>). The insert sequence at 0x4D3487..0x4D34D7 is a literal DynamicVectorClass<T*>::Add: [0x8B3DC8] is compared with [0x8B3DD0] (Capacity vs Count), [0x8B3DD4] is added as the CapacityIncrement, vtable slot +8 is called as Resize, then Count is incremented and the element stored as [ecx+eax*4] = esi, i.e. 4-byte pointer elements. So 0x8B3DD0 counts FootClass-derived objects, which is the correct total-unit count and NOT 0x8B4118.

0x004101F0 disassembles to exactly 5 instructions / 28 bytes (mov [ecx],0x7E1F50; mov [ecx+4],0x7E1F34; mov [ecx+8],0x7E1F2C; mov [ecx+0xC],0x7E1F24; ret), n_callees = 0, and contains zero occurrences of 0xB0F720 / 0xB0F724 / 0xB0F730. All four vftables resolve through [V-4] to CompleteObjectLocators 0x7FB118 / 0x7FB008 / 0x7FAFF0 / 0x7FAFD8, each with signature 0 and TypeDescriptor 0x8177C8 = .?AVAbstractClass@@, at COL offsets 0 / 4 / 8 / 12 respectively. That is the canonical MSVC 4-base multiple-inheritance vptr layout, and it does contradict a "vptr is only at +0" assumption.
